capabilities: Syncs vault files bidirectionally with a Nextcloud folder
Detects changes by content hash and Nextcloud sync-token
Merges conflicting text edits and applies per-file-type conflict strategies
Tracks renames via Nextcloud file IDs and routes deletes through the trashbin
Restores server-side file versions and compares a local file with its remote copy
extras: Requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later and a server certificate the device trusts. Syncing the config folder and selected community plugins is opt-in and marked Dangerous because it copies executable code. No telemetry; credentials are kept in Obsidian's secret storage.
motivation: The author wanted sync built on Nextcloud's own APIs, arguing that most WebDAV sync plugins treat the server as a dumb file store and compare modification times.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to keep a vault in sync with a self-hosted Nextcloud server across desktops and mobile devices.
summary: Bidirectional sync plugin that keeps an Obsidian vault and a Nextcloud folder in step using hash-based change detection and conflict merging.
